title: "Accurate Simulation of Programmable Cloud Laboratories"
date: 2026-06-01
categories: [simulation, automation, cloud-labs, agents]
---

## Problem

Programmable Cloud Laboratories (PCLs) enable remote, automated experimentation at scale, but developing and evaluating orchestration policies on real hardware is slow, expensive, and fault-prone. Reliable simulators are needed to stress-test agents, recover from instrument failures, and benchmark scheduling under realistic lab dynamics.

## Approach

I am building **CloudBench**, an open-framework simulator and benchmark generator for programmable cloud laboratories. The system models instrument state, protocol timing, resource contention, and fault modes so that RL and LLM-based agents can be trained and evaluated before deployment on physical platforms.

## Results

Supports accurate simulation of PCL workflows for orchestration research, including fault recovery and multi-instrument scheduling. Related work includes a contributed talk and poster at the [AI Scientist Summer Workshop](https://ai-scientist-workshop.github.io/#about) (Microsoft Research, Cambridge MA, 2026).

## Status

Manuscript in preparation (*CloudBench: An Open-Framework Simulator and Benchmark Generator for Programmable Cloud Laboratories*). Code and benchmarks will be released with the paper.
